title: Make a Repo & Push
subtitle: Create on GitHub, connect remote, push
description: Part 3 of Git & GitHub — create your own repository, wire up a remote, and push commits so your work lives on GitHub.
learningOutcomes: Create a new repository on GitHub
Get a local project ready for git (init or existing folder)
Connect the local repo to the GitHub remote
Push commits so they appear on GitHub
Confirm the code is visible on the GitHub repo page

goals.title: Create a repository
goals.goal: Create a new repository on GitHub (empty is fine).
goals.coachAsk: Help me create a new repository on GitHub. I'm signed in or ready to sign in — point at how to start a new repo and what to fill in at a high level.
goals.doneWhen: A new GitHub repository page exists (can be empty), or the create-repo form was completed.
tips: You can skip README if you already have local files

goals.title: Prepare a local project
goals.goal: Have a local folder that is a git repo (git init or an existing project) ready to connect.
goals.coachAsk: Help me get a local folder ready as a git repo — either init a new one with a simple file, or use a project I already have. No push yet.
goals.doneWhen: A local directory is a git repository with at least one commit (or clearly ready to connect).
tips: A folder with a single README is enough
You can reuse work from Git on Your Mac

goals.title: Connect the remote
goals.goal: Add the GitHub repo as the remote for your local project.
goals.coachAsk: How do I connect my local git repo to the GitHub repo I just created? Walk me through adding the remote — look at my screen for Terminal or GitHub's suggested commands.
goals.doneWhen: A remote pointing at the GitHub repo is configured (e.g. git remote -v shows it), or the learner confirmed it's set.
tips: GitHub often shows the exact commands after create
HTTPS or SSH both work — pick what you can auth with

goals.title: Push to GitHub
goals.goal: Push your local commits so they land on GitHub.
goals.coachAsk: Help me push my local commits to GitHub. If auth pops up, coach me through whatever's on screen without assuming one login method.
goals.doneWhen: Push succeeded, or GitHub shows the commits/files from the local repo.
tips: Auth prompts are normal the first time
If push fails, read the error together — don't panic

goals.title: Confirm it's online
goals.goal: Open the GitHub repo page and see your files or latest commit there.
goals.coachAsk: Show me how to confirm my code is actually on GitHub — point at the repo page proof that the push worked.
goals.doneWhen: The GitHub repository page shows the pushed files or commit.
tips: Refresh the repo page if it still looks empty
You're done when you can see your stuff online
